question: Where did the drug that made organ transplants routine in the 1980s come from?
answer: A bag of Norwegian soil. In 1969 a Sandoz biologist, Hans Peter Frey, collected soil samples on holiday on the Hardangervidda plateau. A fungus from one, Tolypocladium inflatum, made a compound that disappointed as an antifungal; in 1972 Jean-François Borel found it damped the immune system. It became ciclosporin.
move: A compound that fails one test deserves to meet a different one.
source: Svarstad et al., Biodiversity and Conservation, 2000
reference: Svarstad, Bugge & Dhillion, From Norway to Novartis: cyclosporin from Tolypocladium inflatum in an open access bioprospecting regime, Biodiversity and Conservation, 2000
